title: Royal Enfield Posts Record Festive Sales of 2.67 Lakh Motorcycles
excerpt: October sales rose 7 per cent to 1,33,442 units as exports jumped 47 per cent, taking September-October festive sales to a company-high 2,67,400 units.
body:
• Royal Enfield sold 1,33,442 motorcycles in October 2026, up 7 per cent from 1,24,951 a year earlier, its highest-ever monthly total in the reports.
  • Festive sales across September and October reached 2,67,400 units, surpassing last year's entire festive-season total before this season had closed.
  • Exports jumped 47 per cent to 11,915 units in October, while domestic sales rose 4 per cent to 1,21,527 units.
  • For investors tracking Eicher Motors, April-October sales are up 18 per cent to 8,42,538 units, with Motoverse 2026 and the Himalayan 750 debut next on the calendar.

Royal Enfield sold 1,33,442 motorcycles in October 2026, a 7 per cent increase from 1,24,951 units in October 2025, according to the company's sales figures reported by GaadiWaadi and Acko Drive. The bigger figure was the festive tally: combined sales across September and October reached 2,67,400 motorcycles, which the company described as its best-ever festive performance.

That two-month total had already surpassed Royal Enfield's sales for the whole of last year's festive season before the current season had ended, both reports said. The company attributed the response to demand across its portfolio, from established models to newer additions.

"It has been an exceptional festive season for us at Royal Enfield. Riders across the country continue to choose our brand and motorcycles, making this our best-ever festive performance."

— B. Govindarajan, Managing Director of Eicher Motors and CEO of Royal Enfield

Domestic growth, a faster rise in exports

Domestic sales in October were 1,21,527 units, up 4 per cent from 1,16,844 units a year earlier. Exports rose far faster, climbing 47 per cent to 11,915 units from 8,107 units in October 2025. In other words, most of October's headline growth rate came from international markets, even though India still accounted for the overwhelming share of volume.

Govindarajan pointed to the same spread of demand in his comments, citing "iconic favourites like the Classic 350 to new additions like the Himalayan 440," according to Acko Drive. GaadiWaadi also named the Classic 350 and Himalayan 440 among the motorcycles that played a key role in festive sales.

Seven months into the financial year

For April to October, the first seven months of FY27, Royal Enfield sold 8,42,538 motorcycles, up 18 per cent from 7,16,854 units in the corresponding period of FY26. Domestic sales over that period grew 20 per cent to 7,63,548 units, from 6,38,326 units a year earlier. Exports over the seven months were nearly flat, rising 1 per cent to 78,990 units from 78,528 units, which makes October's 47 per cent export jump a one-month acceleration rather than the pattern for the year so far.

A limited run also tested demand at the top of the range. The Classic 650 125th Anniversary Edition Hypershift, limited to 125 units for India, sold out in less than six minutes, Acko Drive reported. GaadiWaadi reported the same allocation sold in less than 6 minutes and described colour-shifting paint across red, green and gold, a gilded 125-year crest and hand-painted pinstripes.

Beyond the petrol range

Royal Enfield's electric mobility brand, Flying Flea, expanded its retail operations to Hyderabad and Pune during the period. Acko Drive reported the brand entered Hyderabad with one company-operated store and three additional outlets, followed by 10 sales and service touchpoints in Pune. GaadiWaadi reported Hyderabad gained one company store and three additional outlets and Pune added ten sales and service centres, following the brand's earlier entry into Bengaluru.

What to watch next

The next date on the company's calendar is Motoverse 2026 in November, where, GaadiWaadi reported, the Himalayan 750 will make its local debut. For readers holding Eicher Motors shares or planning a purchase, the questions that follow from October's figures are whether exports sustain October's pace after a flat seven months, and whether domestic demand holds after the festive peak that produced the record.
